title: The mate of an isomorphism along equivalences is an isomorphism
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal C',\mathcal D'$ be categories, let
$L\dashv R$ be an adjunction with $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$
(unit $\eta$, counit $\varepsilon$), let $L'\dashv R'$ be an adjunction with
$L':\mathcal C'\to\mathcal D'$, $R':\mathcal D'\to\mathcal C'$ (unit $\eta'$, counit
$\varepsilon'$), let $G:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'$ and $G':\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ be
functors, and let $\theta:L'G\xrightarrow{\sim}G'L$ be a natural isomorphism. Let

$$
 \alpha:GR\xrightarrow{\ \eta'GR\ }R'L'GR\xrightarrow{\ R'\theta R\ }R'G'LR
 \xrightarrow{\ R'G'\varepsilon\ }R'G'
$$

be the mate of $\theta$. If $G$ is an equivalence of categories (fully faithful and
essentially surjective) and $G'$ is fully faithful, then $\alpha$ is a natural
isomorphism.

source.place: no statement in the document: the abstract fact behind 'agit par transport de structure' of Deligne, La conjecture de Weil II, (1.1.7) p. 151 and (1.1.14) p. 153, as used for the exchange maps of the Frobenius square in lem-weil-frobenius-cohomology-transport-iso; written by an agent (standard reference on mates, Kelly-Street, Review of the elements of 2-categories, LNM 420, section 2.2, is not in literature/)

proof.text: Fix $d\in\mathcal D$. For $c\in\mathcal C$, full faithfulness means that $G$ and $G'$ induce bijections on the relevant Hom sets. The adjunctions, by definition, give bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(c,Rd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lc,d)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(L'Gc,G'd)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,R'G'd)$. Precomposition with the invertible arrow $\theta_c$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}(G'Lc,G'd)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}(L'Gc,G'd)$, with inverse precomposition with $\theta_c^{-1}$. Thus their composite $B_{c,d}:\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,GRd)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,R'G'd)$ is bijective. No assertion about preservation of isomorphisms by mates is used here.

source.place: Agent proof of the abstract mate lemma; context: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), p. 151, and (1.1.14), p. 153 (these passages motivate transport but do not state this abstract lemma). Step 1

proof.text: For $\varphi:Gc\to GRd$, let $t:c\to Rd$ be its unique preimage under $G$, so $\varphi=G(t)$. Write the adjunction bijections explicitly: the transpose of $t$ is $\varepsilon_d\circ L(t)$, and the transpose of $h:L'Gc\to G'd$ is $R'(h)\circ\eta'_{Gc}$. Consequently $B_{c,d}(G(t))=R'(G'(\varepsilon_d)\circ G'L(t)\circ\theta_c)\circ\eta'_{Gc}$. These formulas are part of the unit-counit description of the given adjunctions (their inverse formulas are $h\mapsto R(h)\circ\eta_c$ and $u\mapsto\varepsilon'_{G'd}\circ L'(u)$, respectively).

source.place: Agent proof of the abstract mate lemma; context: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), p. 151, and (1.1.14), p. 153 (these passages motivate transport but do not state this abstract lemma). Step 2

proof.text: Naturality of $\theta$ at $t$ gives $G'L(t)\circ\theta_c=\theta_{Rd}\circ L'G(t)$; naturality of $\eta'$ at $G(t)$ gives $R'L'G(t)\circ\eta'_{Gc}=\eta'_{GRd}\circ G(t)$. Substitute these two equalities into Step 2 and use functoriality and associativity. The result is $B_{c,d}(\varphi)=R'G'(\varepsilon_d)\circ R'(\theta_{Rd})\circ\eta'_{GRd}\circ\varphi=\alpha_d\circ\varphi$. Therefore postcomposition with $\alpha_d$ is bijective on morphisms whose source is $Gc$.

source.place: Agent proof of the abstract mate lemma; context: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), p. 151, and (1.1.14), p. 153 (these passages motivate transport but do not state this abstract lemma). Step 3

proof.text: For any $x\in\mathcal C'$, essential surjectivity supplies $c\in\mathcal C$ and an isomorphism $u:Gc\xrightarrow{\sim}x$. Precomposition with $u$ is a bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(x,z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(Gc,z)$ for either $z=GRd$ or $z=R'G'd$, with inverse precomposition with $u^{-1}$. Associativity gives $(\alpha_d\circ f)\circ u=\alpha_d\circ(f\circ u)$. Hence postcomposition with $\alpha_d$ is bijective on $\operatorname{Hom}(x,GRd)\to\operatorname{Hom}(x,R'G'd)$ for every $x$. This is just composition of the three bijections, not an invocation of Yoneda.

source.place: Agent proof of the abstract mate lemma; context: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), p. 151, and (1.1.14), p. 153 (these passages motivate transport but do not state this abstract lemma). Step 4

proof.text: Set $a=GRd$, $b=R'G'd$. Surjectivity in Step 4 at $x=b$ gives $\beta_d:b\to a$ with $\alpha_d\circ\beta_d=\operatorname{id}_b$. At $x=a$, the two maps $\beta_d\circ\alpha_d$ and $\operatorname{id}_a$ have the same image under postcomposition with $\alpha_d$, since $\alpha_d\circ\beta_d\circ\alpha_d=\alpha_d$. Injectivity in Step 4 gives $\beta_d\circ\alpha_d=\operatorname{id}_a$. Thus every component $\alpha_d$ is invertible.

source.place: Agent proof of the abstract mate lemma; context: Deligne, Weil II (1.1.7), p. 151, and (1.1.14), p. 153 (these passages motivate transport but do not state this abstract lemma). Step 5

proof.text: For $f:d\to e$, counit naturality gives $f\circ\varepsilon_d=\varepsilon_e\circ LR(f)$, naturality of $\theta$ gives $G'LR(f)\circ\theta_{Rd}=\theta_{Re}\circ L'GR(f)$, and unit naturality gives $R'L'GR(f)\circ\eta'_{GRd}=\eta'_{GRe}\circ GR(f)$. Applying $R'G'$ to the first equality and $R'$ to the second, functoriality and associativity give the explicit calculation $$R'G'(f)\circ\alpha_d=R'(G'(f\circ\varepsilon_d)\circ\theta_{Rd})\circ\eta'_{GRd}=R'(G'(\varepsilon_e)\circ G'LR(f)\circ\theta_{Rd})\circ\eta'_{GRd}=R'(G'(\varepsilon_e)\circ\theta_{Re})\circ R'L'GR(f)\circ\eta'_{GRd}=\alpha_e\circ GR(f).$$ Thus the displayed mate is natural. Compose this equation on the left with $\beta_e$ and on the right with $\beta_d$; the two inverse equations of Step 5 give $\beta_e\circ R'G'(f)=GR(f)\circ\beta_d$. Therefore the component inverses form a natural inverse, proving that $\alpha$ is a natural isomorphism.
